points.text: Primary-task gains modest; error bars overlap Mean Planning in 5 of 7 tasks.
SAC, iCEM, TaCoS used without brief introductions.
Novelty unclear; reward-plus-uncertainty objective not new, integration of existing components.
Algorithm 1 lacks detail on solving objective, rollouts, model updates.
Benchmarks limited; harder and sparse-reward exploration domains absent.
Missing modern exploration-focused baselines such as BRO.
Lambda sensitivity and exploration role insufficiently explored; results contradictory.
Evaluation reports only mean returns and std; should report coverage of true values.
Continuous-time GP-based RL already studied in prior work; novelty incremental.
Figure 2 compares only with mean planner and PETS; more SOTA baselines needed.
Headline claims of scaling, sample efficiency and outperformance exceed evidence.
No main-text numbers quantifying gains.
Guarantees are for GPs while deep experiments use uncalibrated ensembles; model-agnostic wording overreaches.
No limitations section.
Captions omit seeds and error-band definition.
Project link and repository not anonymized.
Appendix 'Theorem 4/5' should read 'Lemma'.
Continuous-time contribution not isolated; no discrete-time bonus baseline or control-rate sweep.
Guarantees' conditions differ from experimental setup; 'model-agnostic' overclaims.
Downstream tasks are reversals; no exploration baselines.
Per-environment lambda optimization criterion unstated.
'Scales better' rests on two low-dimensional runtime ratios.
'More sample-efficient' lacks a sample-efficiency metric.
TaCoS 'fewer interactions' inferred from final returns.
Lemma labels and coefficient inconsistency in proof.
Seeds not stated for Figures 3-4.
Table 3 footnotes mix total and per-episode time.
Finite-difference derivative noise violates i.i.d. sub-Gaussian Assumption 2.
Assumption 2 noise model conflicts with biased, correlated finite-difference derivatives.
No experiments with measurement noise, delay or model mismatch.
Safety and deployment of aggressive exploration not discussed.
Lipschitz/RKHS assumptions unjustified, especially for contact-rich systems.
Benefit of continuous time not shown; no control-rate sweep vs discrete baseline.
Connections to dual/adaptive control could be expanded.
Analyzed algorithm differs from evaluated one: mean model, ensembles, arbitrary lambda, fixed measurements.
OCORL, discrete-time counterpart and strong deep MBRL baselines missing from deep experiments.
Baselines' training budget and tuning parity unstated.
Scalability claim rests on two tiny systems; no dimension sweep.
Table 3 mixes total and per-episode training time.
Seeds unstated; no table of final returns or aggregate CIs.
Sample efficiency never quantified.
Proof steps of Lemma 5 and Theorem 2 unjustified as written.
Theorem 1 assumptions differ between main text and appendix.
Lemma 4 statement omits a factor T.
TaCoS sample efficiency claimed from final returns.
Label and notation inconsistencies in proofs.
Metric used to optimize lambda not stated.
Limitations not stated.
Novelty incremental: transposes prior bonus objective to OCORL framework; proofs follow templates.
Closest prior works not run as baselines; only weaker baselines.
Theorem 2 'first' claim and bound need explicit lambda.
Questionable characterizations of cited works.
Brief related-work characterizations; uncited claim.

P.summary: Modest primary-task gains; overlapping error bars.
Incremental novelty over prior continuous-time and bonus work.
Evaluation metrics inadequate; no coverage rates.

Q.summary: No numeric results tables or aggregate CIs.
Theory does not cover evaluated algorithm; model-agnostic overclaim.
Minor proof labeling and statement inconsistencies.
Downstream evaluation weak; no exploration baselines.
TaCoS interaction claim from final returns.
Proof gaps in Lemma 5 and Theorem 2.
